title: Partial homogenization and target denominator clearing
statement: Let $R$ and $\Lambda$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $\Lambda$, and let $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ be a prime ideal with localization $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $n,m,c\ge0$, $f_j\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m}]$, $a_i\in\Lambda$ for $1\le i\le n$, and $y_i\in\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ for $1\le i\le n+m$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Assume $y_i=a_i/1$ for $i\le n$ and $f_j(y)=0$ for all $j$. There are $d_j\ge0$, polynomials $F_j\in R[x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m},w]$, and values $l_0,l_1,\ldots,l_{n+m},l_w\in\Lambda$ such that: every support monomial $x^e$ of $f_j$ has extra degree $E(e)=\sum_{i>n}e_i\le d_j$; $F_j=\sum_e (f_j)_e\prod_{i=1}^{n+m}x_i^{e_i} w^{d_j-E(e)}$; $l_i=a_i$ for $i\le n$; $l_0,l_w\notin\mathfrak q$; and $l_0F_j(l_1,\ldots,l_{n+m},l_w)=0$ in $\Lambda$ for every $j$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2189–2211, homogenization and the common target annihilator

proof.text: Write the last $m$ values as fractions in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. Choose $w$ to be the product of their denominators and multiply each numerator by the other denominators. Thus all these values have denominator $w\notin\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak)

proof.text: For each $j$, choose $d_j$ as the maximum extra-variable degree of the finite support, zero if the support is empty. Define $F_j$ by the indicated finite monomial sum, with original indices shifted by one to leave room for $x_0$. Assign the first $n$ values to $a_i$, the extra values to the adjusted numerators, and the last to $w$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak)

proof.text: In the localization, every monomial of $F_j$ evaluates to $w^{d_j}$ times the corresponding monomial of $f_j(y)$: the extra denominators cancel against $w^{E(e)}$, with $E(e)\le d_j$. Summing gives zero by the hypothesis on $f_j$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak)

proof.text: The localization zero criterion supplies one annihilator outside $\mathfrak q$ for each unlocalized evaluated $F_j$. Let $l_0$ be their product, or $1$ for an empty family. Primality keeps it outside $\mathfrak q$, and it annihilates every evaluated $F_j$. The displayed equations follow. Empty extra-variable families likewise use denominator $1$.
